findings.title: AssignmentSource datetime cannot be passed through Celery
findings.body: sync_group_assignee_outbound always enqueues sync_assignee_outbound with assignment_source.to_dict(), and that dict includes queued as a datetime. Celery task kwargs are JSON-serialized; datetime is not JSON-serializable, so apply_async raises whenever an inbound webhook sets an AssignmentSource. That is exactly the path this PR adds. The same-integration skip happens only later, inside the worker after should_sync, so the exception fires before any outbound sync: other linked integrations never receive the assignee update, and the originating integration is not cleanly skipped either. from_dict also does not parse an ISO string, so converting queued to a string without a matching parser would drop the source (return None) and re-open the sync loop.

findings.title: queued default is evaluated once at import
findings.body: AssignmentSource.queued defaults to timezone.now() on the dataclass field. That call runs once when the class body is executed, not when each instance is created, so every AssignmentSource built via from_integration or from_dict without an explicit queued value shares the same timestamp from process import. The field is meant to record when the change was queued and is copied into the task payload; it will not reflect the actual assignment time and cannot order or expire rapid successive assignee webhooks.

findings.title: No test that a different integration still syncs
findings.body: The new test only covers the matching-integration case (outbound sync not called). The stated fix is that other issue-sync integrations must still receive the assignee update. Nothing asserts that path, so a regression that suppresses every outbound sync whenever any AssignmentSource is present would still pass.
